headline: High: ms-swift can write and exfiltrate data by default, while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge list with no direct interaction surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest ms-swift output by default. ms-swift has stdin/stdout and file surfaces, but there is no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP bridge documented between the pair.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ms-swift output into a file consumed by awesome-selfhosted, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Use separate workspaces and terminals.
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no runtime, so it is not a leakage source. ms-swift can read/write files and call external APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared workspace or direct data bridge, making leakage contingent on unusual operator setup rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, ms-swift may expose file contents.
IF sensitive files are placed in ms-swift's readable paths and then uploaded via its API calls, leakage increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Store sensitive files outside ms-swift's workspace.
Review allowlisted network destinations before running.
Rotate any tokens placed in ms-swift's handled secrets.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. ms-swift can write files and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and no shared mutable target is documented, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents access to one mutable resource, conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared paths.
Keep git repositories read-only for ms-swift.
requires-engineering: add file locks if shared writes are unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge-management list, not an action-taking agent, so it cannot directly propagate ms-swift errors into downstream actions. ms-swift can emit outputs and call APIs, but there is no documented pipeline where one agent's output is automatically treated as authoritative by the other.
conditions: IF an operator uses ms-swift output as source material for a separate automation, cascading errors become possible.
IF a downstream system treats ms-swift text as authoritative without verification, the risk rises.
mitigations: Require human review of ms-swift outputs.
Do not auto-ingest outputs into other automations.
Add validation checks before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: implement citation or schema verification for generated content.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable open-source list, while ms-swift handles tokens and files and can send data to allowlisted APIs; compliance risk only appears if regulated data is placed into ms-swift's workflows.
conditions: IF PHI, EU PII, or other regulated data is processed through ms-swift, compliance review is required.
IF the operator routes regulated data to allowlisted third-party APIs, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in ms-swift workflows.
Confirm API destinations and data-processing terms.
Keep secrets out of logs and prompts.
requires-engineering: add retention and residency controls to the pipeline.
